topics.topic: Ownership and placement of the pre-export imported-room-name correction rule
questions: Who owns this rule, and must State 3 add it to the rules explicitly placed outside the running instance with no module owner, or assign it to a named module or external component?

quotes:
The owner learns the rule from the governance's rules for writers, read
before the import (R0-79), where the names of imported projects are set
(R0-85); the owner interface does not show it, and Registry promises nothing
of a name the owner writes against it, as for R0-68 and R0-90. The import
renames no room: it stores a picked project's rooms under the names the v1
instance gave them (A16), and a room is never renamed or removed afterwards
(R0-10). So the owner, before making the export on the VPS (R0-72), corrects
there every room name of the projects to be picked that breaks this rule
(owner, 2026-11-23, State 0 round-59 T1). That correction is made in the
legacy v1 instance, by its own means, before the export; the legacy instances
stand outside this document's guarantees (Actors). R0-10's "never renamed or
removed" and R0-12's "cannot be corrected" bind rooms and projects in
Registry, from the import on, and do not reach the legacy instance. The
import then copies names the owner has already checked; it writes no name of
its own and refuses none.
judgement.why: The text assigns the correction to the owner under governance, places its execution in the external legacy instance before export, and expressly excludes any verification or refusal by Registry's import.
